title: Implement centralized comment marker helpers
description:
## Goal
Add `src/comment-markers.js` to centralize hidden marker rendering and parsing for status comments, history comments, runner IDs, session data maps, and linked PR references.

## Required behavior
Export constants for the status/history marker names and helpers such as `renderRunnerIdMarker`, `parseRunnerId`, `renderSessionDataMarker`, `parseSessionData`, and `parseLinkedPrReference`. Parsing must tolerate empty bodies, missing markers, malformed JSON, older comments, and normal Markdown around the markers.

## Rationale
Follow-up runs currently depend on hidden comment state. Duplicated regexes make it easy for a comment copy edit to break continuity. Centralizing this logic makes state reconciliation and comment generation safer.

## Success criteria
Existing comments remain parseable. New render helpers produce the same marker strings currently expected by the action. No GitHub API calls are made in this module.
close_reason: Added centralized comment marker render/parse helpers, rewired call sites, and added tolerance tests

title: Add result comment marker helpers and marker poisoning guards
description:
## Goal
Extend src/comment-markers.js so result comments have a first-class marker API while preserving the PR #17 state-recovery invariants.

## Required changes
- Add RESULT_COMMENT_MARKER_PREFIX for comments shaped like <!-- netlify-agent-run-result:<runner-id>:<session-id> -->.
- Add renderResultCommentMarker({ runnerId, sessionId }) and parseResultCommentIdentifiers(body).
- Validate runner-id and session-id with the existing RUNNER_ID_FORMAT: /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$/.
- Extend ALLOWED_MARKER_INNER so stripUntrustedHtmlComments preserves result markers on read paths.
- Keep result markers non-authoritative: they identify result comments for TOC/listing only and must never feed reconcileAgentState.

## Security considerations
Result comments are bot-authored, so reflected marker-shaped text is dangerous. Any renderer that emits result comments must assert the body contains no STATUS_COMMENT_MARKER, HISTORY_COMMENT_MARKER, RUNNER_ID_MARKER_PREFIX, or SESSION_DATA_MARKER_PREFIX before appending RESULT_COMMENT_MARKER.

## Acceptance criteria
- Existing status/history/runner/session marker parsing still passes.
- Valid result markers round-trip.
- Invalid runner/session ids are rejected.
- stripUntrustedHtmlComments preserves only allowlisted marker shapes.
close_reason: Implemented result comment marker helpers, parser, allowlist support, state-marker guards, and marker tests.

title: Implement comment truncation and status-body assembly primitives
description:
## Goal
Add reusable primitives for short sticky status comments and safe per-result body caps.

## Required module
Create src/comment-truncation.js exporting:
- STATUS_COMMENT_VISIBLE_BYTES = 1000.
- MAX_RESULT_BODY_LENGTH = 60000.
- truncateAtBoundary(text, maxBytes), preferring paragraph break, sentence break, word break, then byte-level fallback.
- assembleStatusBody({ header, subtitle, screenshot, title, links, redirectNote, resultCommentLink, markers, budget }).

## Status rendering contract
Required visible fields are header, run/model/timestamp subtitle, result comment link, redirect note when applicable, and trailing state/status markers. Optional fields are screenshot, title, and compact link row. If the body exceeds budget, drop optional fields in this order: screenshot, title, link row. Never cut inside a markdown link, code fence, or marker.

## Acceptance criteria
- Required fields and markers survive under tight budgets.
- Optional fields are dropped in the documented order.
- Long text truncates at stable boundaries and appends an ellipsis.
- Markers are appended after visible-budget assembly and are never truncated.
close_reason: Implemented comment-truncation primitives, status body assembly, result body cap, and focused tests.

title: Ask mode: answer questions without commits or PRs
description:
## Why
Asking "how does the retry logic in context-service work?" today starts a normal run that may modify files and open a PR. The SDK accepts `mode: 'ask'` on `start` and `followUp` (`RunnerMode = 'normal' | 'create' | 'ask'`, and live sessions echo `"mode": "normal"`), but **the backend semantics of `ask` are undocumented** (not in the SDK README, NAX source, or NAX plans). So the backend contract is probed first (D0).

## Decisions (interview 2026-09-25)
- Ask uses the **repo's normal defaults** (default-agent/default-model-id/default-effort, else Auto) — no separate ask inputs.
- Ask **reuses the thread's runner** (on a PR it sees the branch) — **provisional until D0** confirms normal follow-ups still work after an ask and ask diffs aren't landed.
- Answers use the **result-comment layout** (`Run #N | claude · Fable 5 | answered`, prompt block, `### Answer`) so asks appear in history.

## Syntax (unambiguous forms only)
`@netlify-ask [agent] [model] [effort] question`, `@netlify ask: question` (colon required, selector words may follow), and `mode:ask` in the selector prefix only. A bare leading "ask" is **not** ask mode (`@netlify ask the user to confirm…` is a build request). Dispatch input `runner_mode` (normal|ask), named to avoid colliding with consumer workflows that already use `mode` (e.g. gtm-services uses `mode` for normal/preflight-only/dry-run).

## Behavior
`mode: 'ask'`, landing forced to `none`, **never land** even if `result.changes === 'changed'` (note: "The agent changed files while answering; those changes were not applied."). Scope guard, labels, PR finalization and cross-posting are skipped.

Tests: `bun test src/*.test.js`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run docs:check`. Inline shell in `action.yml` is tested by executing it (`src/action-steps.test.js`). Live verification uses the canary repo `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action-canary` (driven by `.github/workflows/canary.yml`) and the consumer `netlify-labs/gtm-services`.

Source plan: `docs/plans/agent-runner-scope-recovery-release-ask-plan.md` (Workstream D).

title: Scope guard: flag agent changes to protected or unexpected files
description:
## Why (observed evidence)
Live model tests in `gtm-services` on 2026-09-24/25:
| Run | Model | Asked for | PR actually touched |
|---|---|---|---|
| #51 → PR #52 | codex (Auto), low | add `docs/agent-runner-smoke-test.md` | only that file |
| #53 → PR #54 | claude `claude-fable-5`, high | add `docs/agent-runner-fable-smoke-test.md` | that file + `netlify.toml`, `redwood.toml`, `netlify/publish/index.html` |
| #55 → PR #56 | opencode `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, max | add `docs/agent-runner-kimi-smoke-test.md` | that file + `AGENTS.md`, `netlify.toml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml.txt` |

The added files' own comments explain it: the Agent Runners deploy ran `netlify deploy` from the monorepo root, the CLI stopped with "Projects detected: … Configure the project you want to work with", and the agent worked around it. Nothing in the result comment pointed this out; a reviewer could merge deploy-config changes by accident.

## Decisions (interview 2026-09-25)
- **Report, never block by default.** Flags are **comments only** (no GitHub check/commit status); enforcement is left to CODEOWNERS.
- Warnings appear in the result comment **and on the PR** (issue-triggered runs post the section on the PR the run opened/updated; PR-triggered runs post once).
- A flagged file the user's prompt explicitly names (path or basename, or a named folder) is shown as **"Requested"**, not warned.
- A **default scope instruction** is appended to agent prompts (on by default; `scope-instructions: ''` opts out): report unrelated build/deploy failures instead of working around them. This is a minor "Behavior change" under the SemVer policy.

The scope guard (epic EP-A) matches changed file paths against configurable patterns. No new npm dependencies (the runtime is staged with `npm ci --omit=dev`; keep it small and auditable).

## Spec
Match repo-relative POSIX paths:
- `**` any sequence incl. `/`; a leading `**/` also matches zero directories (`**/netlify.toml` matches `netlify.toml`).
- `*` any sequence **without** `/`; `?` one non-`/` char; `{a,b}` alternation (no nesting required).
- A pattern **without `/` matches only at the repo root** (`*.toml`, `AGENTS.md`) — deliberately stricter than `.gitignore`; document prominently.
- `!pattern` negates; evaluate in order; the **last matching** pattern decides.
- Case-sensitive (like git).
API: `compilePatterns(list) → matcher`, `matcher(path) → { matched: boolean, rule: string|null }`; `parsePatternList(input)` splits on newlines/commas, trims, drops empty/comment (`#`) lines, expands the token `default` to the built-in list (exported `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATHS`), and `none` → empty list.

description:

To flag scope creep we need the set of files **this run** changed. Codex review: parsing arbitrary patch text is fragile, so GitHub's file metadata is primary. SDK `RunResult` (success variant) has `diff?: { kind: 'inline', text } | { kind: 'url', url }` — the current session's diff, but the type doesn't promise a complete Git extended-header diff.

## Spec — `src/scope-files.js`
`collectChangedFiles({ github, repo, source }) → { files: [{ path, previousPath?, status: 'added'|'modified'|'removed'|'renamed' }], complete: boolean, reason?: string }` where `source` is one of:
1. `{ kind: 'pr', number }` — new PR opened by this run: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/files`, paginated 100/page; API maximum 3,000 files → `complete:false, reason:'api-cap'` when hit.
2. `{ kind: 'commit', sha }` — follow-up committed to an existing PR: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}`, paginate `files` (cap 3,000).
3. `{ kind: 'diff', text }` — dry run / ask (nothing landed): parse `diff --git` headers + `new file mode`, `deleted file mode`, `rename from`/`rename to`, `similarity index`, `/dev/null` sides, `Binary files … differ`; implement **Git `core.quotePath` C-style unescaping** (quoted paths `"a/…"`, octal escapes for UTF-8 bytes → decode as UTF-8, `\t`, `\n`, `\"`, `\\`); reject malformed headers (→ `complete:false, reason:'malformed-diff'`), never guess.
4. `{ kind: 'url' }` or missing → `{ files: [], complete: false, reason: 'no-file-list' }` (no fetch).

Fixtures: paginated PR files (2 pages), exactly-3000 cap, commit files, quoted paths with spaces/tabs/UTF-8 (`"a/caf\303\251.md"` → `café.md`), renames (both paths kept), deletions, binary, mode-only change, malformed header, empty diff. ## Spec — `src/scope-guard.js`
`evaluateScope({ files, complete, patterns, flagNewTopLevel, prompt, baseTopLevelExists }) → { flags: [{ path, reason, rule }], requested: [path], incomplete?: reason }`
- **Protected**: each changed path (and `previousPath` for renames, deletions included) matched by the compiled patterns → reason `Protected path <rule>`.
- **New top-level** (when `flagNewTopLevel`): added files with no `/` → `New file at the repository root`; for each distinct first segment among added files, `baseTopLevelExists(segment)` (injected; implemented in A5 via `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/{segment}?ref={base}`, 404 ⇒ new) → `New top-level folder` reported once per folder (`netlify/` (new folder)). At most 10 lookups; beyond that add one flag "and N more new top-level entries".
- **Requested**: a flagged path is moved to `requested` if the user's prompt (the cleaned prompt, code spans included — users write `` `netlify.toml` ``) contains the full path, the basename as a whole word (`netlify.toml`), or a named folder prefix (`.github/workflows` covers `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Substring accidents don't count (`toml` alone doesn't suppress `netlify.toml`; match on path-separator/word boundaries).
- Deterministic ordering: protected first, then new-top-level, each sorted by path.

- **Reconstructed fixtures**: PR #54 file list → flags exactly `netlify.toml` (`**/netlify.toml`), `redwood.toml` (`*.toml`), `netlify/` (new folder); PR #56 → `AGENTS.md`, `netlify.toml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml.txt` (new root file); PR #52 → no flags.

title: Run checkpoints, recovery of orphaned runs, and @netlify stop
description:
## Why
If a workflow job is cancelled, times out at job level, loses its runner, or crashes after the agent starts, the Agent Runner keeps working on Netlify but nothing lands its PR and the status comment stays at "manifesting" forever. For a **new** run it is worse: the runner ID reaches the status comment only at the very end (the `Update status to in-progress` step runs only when `steps.extract-agent-id.outputs.agent-runner-id != ''`, i.e. follow-ups). SDK handle checkpoints are written only to `$RUNNER_TEMP`, which dies with the job.

## Decisions (interview 2026-09-25 + Codex review, runner 6ab6c43768ad7de041b2cc8e)
1. **Cancel means stop** the agent (best-effort cleanup step; recovery also treats an owner run with conclusion `cancelled` as a stop).
2. **`job-timeout-minutes` input**: preflight warns and shortens the agent limit to `job-timeout-minutes − 5` so the agent's own deadline fires before GitHub cancels the job (reading YAML was rejected as unreliable).
3. Recovery **reports but does not land** when the PR head moved since the run started; a **closed thread** stops a still-running agent and never lands.
4. **Keep the run's original deadline**; past it, recovery stops the run (SDK: "out-of-band workers must compare the current time to deadlineAt and call stop").
5. The **full SDK handle is stored encrypted** in the status comment (AES-256-GCM, HKDF from `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`, AAD binds repo/thread/runner); fallback rebuild from public fields (tested: rebuilt `run`/`session` handles pass `sdk.parseHandle` when request IDs are UUIDs).
6. **Single writer per thread**: only the job holding the thread's concurrency group writes state, lands, or recovers (comment leases can't lock — GitHub comment updates have no compare-and-swap).
7. **Next-comment recovery** waits for the old run (≤ 40% of the effective agent limit), then runs the new request; else declines with a note.
8. Opt-in **recovery cron** template that only *scans and dispatches* the main workflow per thread (`recover_thread` input).
9. **`@netlify stop`** from comments (exact whole comment), anyone with write access; runs outside the thread group; posts a stop-request reply rather than writing the status comment while the owner lives.
10. Recovered results **@-mention the requester**. Per-run agent/model/effort shown in result/history headers.
11. **Keep one run step** (`netlify-agent`); `run-agent.js` writes the checkpoint itself, so no step outputs move.

description:
## Context

Live verification uses the canary repo `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action-canary` (driven by `.github/workflows/canary.yml`) and the consumer `netlify-labs/gtm-services`.
SDK contract (README "Durable handles and deadlines", line 255): persist the **complete** handle returned by every mutating call; don't construct handles by hand. Handles contain the original prompt, `siteId`, retries, prompt-delivery metadata and landing progress (`prUrl`, `committedSessionIds`, `expectedPrHeadSha`). They must be stored in the (public) status comment without exposing prompt/site ID. GitHub comments are limited to 65,536 characters.

## Spec — `src/checkpoint-crypto.js` (node:crypto only)
- `deriveKey({ token, repo })`: HKDF-SHA256, ikm = `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`, salt = `"<owner>/<repo>"`, info = `"netlify-agent-run-checkpoint/v1"`, 32 bytes.
- `sealHandle({ serializedHandle, key, aad })` → base64url of `nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag(16)`; random nonce per call. `aad = "<owner>/<repo>#<thread number>:<runnerId>"`.
- `openHandle({ sealed, key, aad })` → serialized handle string or throws `CheckpointCryptoError` (`kind: 'auth-failed'|'malformed'|'unknown-version'`).
- `sealForComment({ handle, sdk, key, aad, maxChars = 40000 })`: `sdk.serializeHandle(handle)`; seal; if too long, re-serialize with `input.prompt` and (session) `sessionInput.prompt` replaced by `"[prompt omitted from checkpoint]"` (then `sdk.parseHandle` must still accept it) and seal again; return `{ sealed, promptStripped }`; if still too long throw `kind:'too-large'`.
- Key version constant `KV = 1`.

## Tests (`src/checkpoint-crypto.test.js`)
Round-trip; tampered ciphertext/nonce/tag fail; AAD mismatch (other thread, other runner) fails; wrong token fails; prompt stripping kicks in above the cap and result still `parseHandle`s; output is base64url only; **canary strings**: a handle containing `PROMPT_CANARY_x` and `SITE_CANARY_y` → sealed output contains neither. Performance sanity (< 5 ms for a 40 KB handle).

Live/e2e checks must `echo` each step with a timestamp and write a Markdown table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (scenario, run URL, expectation, observed, pass/fail) so failures are diagnosable from the run page alone.

title: Recovery engine src/recover-run.js (pre-checks, decision table, budgets, rendering)
description:
## Context
Repo: `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action`, a composite GitHub Action (`action.yml`) that starts Netlify Agent Runners from `@netlify` mentions using `nax-agent-runner-sdk@0.3.0`. Live verification uses the canary repo `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action-canary` (driven by `.github/workflows/canary.yml`) and the consumer `netlify-labs/gtm-services`.
Recovery finishes runs whose owning job died. It **only ever runs inside a job holding the thread's concurrency group** (single writer; see B2d). SDK: `getSnapshot` (non-blocking), `waitFor`, `land` (resumable from handle landing progress), `stop`; out-of-band workers must stop runs past `deadlineAt`.

## Spec
`recoverRun({ sdk, github, repo, thread, statusComment, checkpoint, input, budgetMs, now, signal }) → { outcome: 'finalized'|'stopped'|'still-running'|'skipped', reason, sessionDataMap }`
1. **Handle**: `openHandle` (B1a); on failure `buildResumeHandle` (B2a). Cross-check decrypted handle `runnerId`/`currentSessionId`/`siteId` against public fields and configured site → mismatch = skip with warning.
2. **Pre-checks in order**: owner run (`GET /actions/runs/{ghRunId}`) still queued/in_progress → skip; owner conclusion `cancelled` → `sdk.stop` if active, post "Stopped: the workflow was cancelled" → `stopped`; thread closed (issue closed, PR closed/merged) → stop if active, never land, post "Stopped: this thread was closed before the run finished" → `stopped`; `stop-pending` → retry stop → `stopped`; `now ≥ deadlineAt` and active → `sdk.stop`, timed-out result → `stopped`.
3. **Snapshot table**: succeeded+changes+not landed+PR head unchanged (`prHeadSha`) → `sdk.land`, persist returned handle (re-seal checkpoint) → render → `finalized`; PR head moved → don't land, result says "Not applied: the branch changed after this run started. See the agent run to apply it manually." → `finalized`; succeeded already landed/no changes → render → `finalized`; failed/cancelled → failure render → `finalized`; active before deadline → `sdk.waitFor` with this job's budget via `AbortSignal` (handle `deadlineAt` NOT modified), re-decide; still active → `still-running` (state stays `running`).
4. **Rendering** reuses `renderResultComment` (header suffix `· recovered`; body starts "@<requester>, your earlier request finished."), `renderStatusComment`, `renderHistoryTocFromComments`; writes `agent-sessions-<runnerId>.json` like run-agent.
5. **Idempotency**: skip result comment if `parseResultCommentIdentifiers` finds this sessionId already.

## Tests (`src/recover-run.test.js`, fake transport like `run-agent.test.js` `dryRunTransport`)
Every pre-check and table row; decrypt failure → rebuild path; mismatch skip; deadline arithmetic with injected `now`; AbortSignal budget honored and `deadlineAt` unchanged; moved PR head; requester mention; idempotent rerun; closed PR vs merged PR.
Test logging: every new test file prints nothing on success, but assertion messages must name the input case (`assert.equal(actual, expected, JSON.stringify(input))`). Live/e2e checks must `echo` each step with a timestamp and write a Markdown table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (scenario, run URL, expectation, observed, pass/fail) so failures are diagnosable from the run page alone.

title: Opt-in recovery cron template and docs
description:
## Context
Repo: `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action`, a composite GitHub Action (`action.yml`) that starts Netlify Agent Runners from `@netlify` mentions using `nax-agent-runner-sdk@0.3.0`. Live verification uses the canary repo `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action-canary` (driven by `.github/workflows/canary.yml`) and the consumer `netlify-labs/gtm-services`.
Users asked what "the sweeper" is — docs must explain it plainly: an **optional second workflow file** GitHub starts on a timer (`on: schedule`); it doesn't react to comments; it finds agent runs whose GitHub job died and asks the main workflow to finish them. Without it, orphans finish only on the next `@netlify` comment in that thread.

## Spec
`workflow-templates/netlify-agents-recover.yml` (+ `.properties.json` entry):
```yaml
on:
  schedule: [{ cron: '*/30 * * * *' }]
  workflow_dispatch:
concurrency: { group: netlify-agents-recover-scan, cancel-in-progress: false }
permissions: { contents: read, issues: read, pull-requests: read, actions: write }
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: netlify-labs/agent-runner-action@v1
        with:
          operation: recover-scan
          recover-workflow: netlify-agents.yml
          netlify-auth-token: ${{ secrets.NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          netlify-site-id: ${{ secrets.NETLIFY_SITE_ID }}
```
README section: what it does, example scenario (runner lost at minute 8, PR appears within 30 min), cost (~20–30 s per empty scan ≈ 15–25 Actions minutes/day at */30), GitHub caveats (schedules can be delayed; disabled in public repos after 60 days of inactivity), permissions rationale.

## Tests
actionlint; docs drift for new inputs.
close_reason: workflow-templates/netlify-agents-recover.yml (+ properties.json): opt-in schedule */30 + workflow_dispatch, scan concurrency group, read-only permissions + actions: write, operation: recover-scan; README 'Recovering unfinished runs' explains next-comment recovery and the cron in plain terms with cost and GitHub schedule caveats.

`src/run-agent.js` `runAgentAction()` calls `sdk.start` (new) or `createLegacyHandle` + `sdk.followUp` (follow-up), saves `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-runner-sdk-handle-<runnerId>.json` via `saveHandleCheckpoint` (also from the SDK `onLandingCheckpoint` hook), then `waitFor` → `land`. The step `Update status to in-progress` (action.yml) only runs for follow-ups, so **new runs never show the runner link or a durable runner ID until the end**. Codex review: splitting run-agent into start/finish steps would move outputs between step IDs and break every `steps.netlify-agent.outputs.*` reference — so keep **one step** and write the checkpoint from inside run-agent.

- Test-only input `simulate-orphan` (action input, default `false`, documented as test-only): when `true`, exit 0 right after the first checkpoint write **without** waiting, leaving `state: running` (used by the orphan-recovery canary).
- All existing outputs and failure paths unchanged; the crash-fallback wrapper unchanged.

description:
## Context

Decision: cancelling the workflow means stop the agent. GitHub runs `if: cancelled()` steps on manual cancel (and on job timeout, which is why B1f exists), but cleanup is **best-effort**: a lost runner runs nothing; grace periods can expire. Recovery (B2b) therefore also treats an owner run with conclusion `cancelled` as stop.

## Spec
New step `Stop agent on cancel` with `if: cancelled() && steps.install-deps.outputs.action-dir != ''`, github-script requiring `${{ACTION_DIR}}/src/stop-on-cancel.js`:
- Load the newest `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-runner-sdk-handle-*.json`; none → no-op (log "no active run").
- `sdk.stop(handle)`; then update the status comment: checkpoint `state: stopped`, body "⏹ The workflow was cancelled, so the agent run was stopped." + links.
- Stop call fails → checkpoint `state: stop-pending` (next thread job retries).
- One stop attempt + one comment update, total timeout ~20 s (abort signal), nothing else.

## Tests
- Module tests with fake SDK/github: stop ok → `stopped`; stop throws → `stop-pending`; no handle file → no-op; comment update failure is logged, not thrown.
- action-steps test: condition string exact, loads from `ACTION_DIR`, placed after the run step and before comment generation.
- Covered live by B1h.
Test logging: every new test file prints nothing on success, but assertion messages must name the input case (`assert.equal(actual, expected, JSON.stringify(input))`). Live/e2e checks must `echo` each step with a timestamp and write a Markdown table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (scenario, run URL, expectation, observed, pass/fail) so failures are diagnosable from the run page alone.

description:
## Context

When a job hits its own `timeout-minutes`, GitHub cancels it and `cancelled()` steps run — indistinguishable from a human cancel, so the agent would be stopped (cancel = stop). Prevent it: make the agent's limit (`timeout-minutes` input, default 10; max `MAX_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` 24h in run-agent) always fit inside the job. Codex review: reading `timeout-minutes` from workflow YAML is unreliable (expressions, matrices, reusable workflows, ref vs sha), so use an explicit input.

## Spec
- New input `job-timeout-minutes` (default `''`).
- Preflight (`src/preflight.js` + action step): when set and `timeout-minutes + 5 > job-timeout-minutes`, add a warning check (`job-timeout`) and set an output `effective-timeout-minutes = job-timeout-minutes − 5` (min 1); when empty, add an info line to the step summary suggesting setting it. Warnings go to annotations + step summary only (never comments).
- `MAX_WAIT_MINUTES` for the run step uses `steps.preflight.outputs.effective-timeout-minutes || inputs.timeout-minutes`.
- Templates (`workflow-templates/netlify-agents.yml`, `example-workflow.yml`, dogfood, and docs) set `job-timeout-minutes` equal to the job's `timeout-minutes`.

## Tests
Preflight table tests (unset, fits, too tight, invalid values); action-steps test for the MAX_WAIT_MINUTES expression; docs drift for the new input.

## Context

`.github/workflows/canary.yml` today runs one fixed scenario: it pins the canary repo's `netlify-agents.yml` to the PR head SHA, opens an issue with `DEFAULT_PROMPT="@netlify codex mini low in README.md, replace or add one line exactly: Canary marker: ${RUN_MARKER}. Do not edit other files."`, waits for the downstream run, and asserts success + a PR whose diff contains the marker. Several workstreams need **additional live scenarios** (scope creep, cancel stops, orphan recovery, stop command, ask), each with its own prompt, mid-run actions, and assertions.

## Goal
Add a `scenario` input (workflow_dispatch and workflow_call) with values `default` (today's behavior, still what PR-triggered canaries run), plus slots for `scope-creep`, `cancel-stops`, `orphan-recovery`, `stop-command`, `ask`. Structure the controller so each scenario is a small bash function (`scenario_<name>_prompt`, `scenario_<name>_during` for mid-run actions such as cancelling the downstream run or posting a comment, `scenario_<name>_assert`). Scenarios whose feature hasn't shipped yet fail fast with "scenario not implemented" so the menu can grow bead by bead.

## Details
- Keep `default` byte-for-byte compatible for the PR path (`pull_request` trigger); CI must stay green.
- Shared helpers: `wait_for_run_start`, `wait_for_run_complete`, `find_pr_from_issue`, `status_comment_body` (bot-authored comment containing `<!-- netlify-agent-run-status -->`), `checkpoint_state` (parse `<!-- netlify-agent-run-checkpoint:{json} -->` `state` with `jq`), `backend_session_config <runnerId>` (GET `https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/agent_runners/<id>/sessions` with `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` secret, print `agent_config` + state).
- Needs a `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` secret in the source repo for backend assertions (document in the canary README section of AGENTS.md).
- Cleanup: closing canary issues/PRs remains the canary repo's weekly cleanup workflow's job.

## Acceptance
- `default` behaves exactly as before (PR canary passes on this bead's PR).
- `gh workflow run canary.yml -f scenario=default` works; unimplemented scenarios fail with a clear message.
- Summary table per scenario (see logging).

## Tests
- Unit-test the jq/bash helpers by extracting them to `scripts/canary-lib.sh` and executing them in `src/action-steps.test.js`-style tests with fixture JSON (status comment bodies with/without checkpoint markers, session API payloads).

title: Parse mentions into one command object (command, mode, selection, prompt)
description:
## Context
Repo: `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action`, a composite GitHub Action (`action.yml`) that starts Netlify Agent Runners from `@netlify` mentions using `nax-agent-runner-sdk@0.3.0`. Runtime code is staged into `$RUNNER_TEMP/netlify-agent-runner-action` by the `install-deps` step; every later step loads it via `ACTION_DIR`. Tests: `bun test src/*.test.js`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run docs:check`. Inline shell in `action.yml` is tested by executing it (`src/action-steps.test.js`). Live verification uses the canary repo `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action-canary` (driven by `.github/workflows/canary.yml`) and the consumer `netlify-labs/gtm-services`.
`src/utils.js` parses mentions with `parseMentionLine` / `parseSelection` / `resolveSelection` / `stripSelection` (agent → model → effort tokenizer, catalog in `src/agent-catalog.js`, explicit `model:`/`effort:` tokens anywhere on the `@netlify` line). `src/get-context.js` builds `triggerText` and **appends a source-URL line** (`\n\n◌ <url>`) before outputs are produced. Upcoming features need two new concepts in the same grammar: a **command** (`stop`, Workstream B) and a **mode** (`ask`, Workstream D). Codex's review found the grammar lacked one normalized contract (e.g. `ask:` currently stops selector parsing and becomes prompt text; `mode:ask` could be ordinary prose; stop semantics undefined for non-comment events).

## Goal
Introduce a single parsed object from the **first triggering mention line**, parsed **before** source-URL decoration:
```js
{ command: 'run' | 'stop', mode: 'normal' | 'ask', selection: { agent, model, effort }, prompt, explicit: { model, effort, mode } }
```
This bead only builds the structure and wires `command:'run'`/`mode:'normal'` everywhere (no user-visible change). Stop (B) and ask (D) plug into it later.

## Details
- New `parseCommand(text, { eventName })` in `src/utils.js` returning the object; `get-context.js` calls it on the raw trigger/selection text (issue title handling via `selectionText` stays as today) and exposes outputs `command`, `runner-mode` (always `normal` for now).
- Keep **existing** explicit-token behavior: `model:`/`effort:` count anywhere on the `@netlify` line (narrowing them would change how existing mentions resolve = breaking under SemVer policy). New tokens (`mode:`) will be prefix-only — implement the "selector prefix" boundary helper now (`selectorPrefixEnd(line)`), unused by existing tokens.
- Dispatch precedence rule documented in code: dispatch inputs (`agent`, `model_id`, `effort`, later `runner_mode`) override mention words.
- No behavior change: all 601+ existing tests must pass unchanged.

## Acceptance
- `parseCommand` exists, is used by `get-context.js`, and existing outputs are identical for the full current test corpus (add a golden test that runs every mention in `src/agent-selection.test.js` cases through both old and new paths and compares agent/model/effort/cleaned prompt).
- `tsc` clean; docs unchanged.

## Tests
- Golden parity test above; unit tests for `selectorPrefixEnd` (after trigger + selector words + optional `:`/`,`/sentence `.`), CRLF bodies, code-span stripping, source-URL line never parsed.
- Test logging: every new test file prints nothing on success, but assertion messages must name the input case (`assert.equal(actual, expected, JSON.stringify(input))`). Live/e2e checks must `echo` each step with a timestamp and write a Markdown table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (scenario, run URL, expectation, observed, pass/fail) so failures are diagnosable from the run page alone.
close_reason: utils.parseCommand -> {command, mode, selection, prompt, explicit} parsed from the raw trigger text before the source-URL line; selectorPrefixEnd helper for prefix-only tokens; get-context outputs command + runner-mode (run/normal for now). Parity test over the selection corpus: identical agent/model/effort and cleaned prompt.

title: Versioned releases with a moving v1 tag
description:
## Why
The README and every workflow template tell consumers `uses: netlify-labs/agent-runner-action@v1`, but the repo has **no tags at all** (`git ls-remote --tags origin` is empty), so `@v1` does not resolve. Every consumer pins a commit SHA by hand (`gtm-services` was bumped manually three times on 2026-09-24/25). Releases make `@v1` real, let Dependabot propose upgrades, and give every later feature (scope guard, recovery, stop, ask) a versioned home.

## Decisions (interview 2026-09-25)
- Immutable SemVer tags `vX.Y.Z`; a moving major tag `v1` always points at the latest `v1.Y.Z`.
- First release **`v1.0.0`** = the merge commit of the release-workflow PR.
- Releases are cut by **manual `workflow_dispatch`** of `release.yml` with a `version` input and `dry_run` (default `true`), gated on tests + a live canary. **No approval environment** — the canary is the gate.
- `gtm-services` will pin `@<sha> # vX.Y.Z` and use Dependabot's `github-actions` ecosystem (reviewed PRs, nothing moves under a production repo silently). The example repo moves from `@main` to `@v1`. The canary repo keeps SHA pins (it tests exact commits).
- **SemVer policy:** *breaking* (needs v2) = changes that break a consumer workflow or stored state: removing/renaming an input or output, changing an input's accepted values, changing comment-marker formats so old/new versions can't read each other, or changing mention grammar so previously valid mentions resolve to a different agent/model/effort. *Minor* = additive inputs/outputs, new markers old versions ignore, new mention forms that were previously plain prompt text, and changes to agent guidance or comment content (listed under **"Behavior changes"** in notes). Workflow-file updates needed only for new features go under **"Action required to use new features"**.

## Scope
Children: reusable canary (`workflow_call`), version-validation module, `release.yml`, actionlint in CI, docs/policy, tag rulesets, then cutting v1.0.0 and migrating consumers. This epic closes the pre-existing bead `agent-runner-action-o70` ("Release gate before moving @main or release tags"), whose required checks become the release checklist.

Live verification uses the canary repo `netlify-labs/agent-runner-action-canary` (driven by `.github/workflows/canary.yml`) and the consumer `netlify-labs/gtm-services`.

Source plan: `docs/plans/agent-runner-scope-recovery-release-ask-plan.md` (Workstream C). Beads are self-contained; the plan is background only.

`.github/workflows/canary.yml` triggers on `pull_request` (paths `action.yml`, `src/**`) and `workflow_dispatch` (inputs `action_ref`, `canary_repo`, `canary_workflow_path`, `canary_workflow_name`, `timeout_minutes`, `prompt`, `simulate_failure`). - Concurrency: a reusable workflow's `concurrency` is evaluated in the caller's context, so `canary-${{ github.ref }}` would put release.yml's canary in the same group as a manual canary on `main`. Make the group `canary-${{ inputs.action_ref || github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.ref }}` so each tested commit gets its own group.

## Acceptance
- PR canary still runs and passes on this bead's own PR.
- A throwaway caller workflow on a branch (`uses: ./.github/workflows/canary.yml` with `action_ref: ${{ github.sha }}`, `secrets: inherit`) succeeds; remove the throwaway before merge or keep it as `canary-call-smoke.yml` behind workflow_dispatch.

title: Implement durable agent state reconciliation
description:
## Goal
Add `src/state-reconciliation.js` to reconstruct the best known Netlify Agent state from status comment body, PR body, linked PR hints, existing outputs, and site/runner metadata.

## Required behavior
Return a structured result with `runnerId`, `sessionDataMap`, `linkedPrNumber`, `agentRunUrl`, `confidence`, `sources`, `warnings`, and `recoveryAction`. Prefer valid status comment state over PR body fallback. Treat malformed session JSON as a warning, not a crash. Distinguish no state from broken state.

## Rationale
Follow-up prompts and issue-to-PR redirects depend on recovering state from comments that users or bots may edit or delete. A pure reconciliation layer lets the action recover consistently and gives scenario tests a stable assertion point.

## Success criteria
The module is pure and independently testable. It preserves current behavior for valid comments while adding safer fallback and warning behavior for malformed or partial state.
close_reason: Implemented pure state reconciliation module with tests

title: Add scenario harness and simulator coverage for thread-history lifecycle
description:
## Goal
Extend scenario-harness/simulator coverage so the multi-comment lifecycle is validated at workflow level, not only helper level.

## Required scenarios
- Three sequential triggers on the same PR: one mutable status comment, three immutable result comments, one newest-first TOC with three rows.
- Issue-to-PR handoff: issue gets status+result with redirect note; PR gets PR-local status+result+one-row TOC.
- State recovery with result comments present: extract-agent-id recovers runner/session data only from the status comment and ignores result comments.
- Poisoned result comment: non-bot fake result marker and fake state markers do not affect state recovery and do not appear in TOC.
- Result comment create failure: status update still happens in degraded mode and summary/debug output makes the problem visible.

## Acceptance criteria
Scenario traces make comment create/update/list operations inspectable with enough logging to debug ordering mistakes.

title: Build truncated status comment renderer
description:
## Goal

## Required behavior

- Render a concise status body with header, run/model/timestamp subtitle, optional screenshot/title/link row, required result link, optional issue-to-PR redirect note, and trailing SESSION_DATA_MARKER, RUNNER_ID_MARKER, STATUS_COMMENT_MARKER.

- Preserve session-data-map round-tripping from generate-success-comment/extract-agent-id.

Only the status comment carries RUNNER_ID_MARKER, SESSION_DATA_MARKER, and STATUS_COMMENT_MARKER. Result and history comments must not carry those markers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Status bodies stay within the 1000-byte visible budget for representative success and error inputs.
- Result link is always present when a result comment exists.

title: Post immutable result comments and expose comment ids
description:
## Goal
Add src/post-result-comment.js and action wiring support for creating immutable result comments before updating sticky status comments.

## Required behavior
- Call github.rest.issues.createComment with result-body.
- Set result-comment-id and result-comment-url outputs.
- Skip cleanly when result-body is empty, so preflight/setup failures and no-session failures remain status-only.
- Use the same github-token permissions and issue-number context as existing comment steps.
- Mark the step continue-on-error so comment delivery failures do not fail an otherwise completed agent run.

## Degraded behavior
If createComment fails, the run should still update the status comment using a degraded single-comment body or a clear notice that result comment posting failed. The step summary should make this visible.

## Acceptance criteria

- Failed createComment does not break fallback status reporting.

title: Preserve failure, fallback, and no-session behavior
description:
## Goal
Make the new lifecycle robust across success, dry-run, mid-run failure, preflight failure, generator failure, and result-comment posting failure.

## Required behavior
- Preflight/setup failures without a Netlify session produce status comments only.
- Mid-run failures with validated runner-id and latest session-id produce both result and status comments.
- If result comment posting fails, status reporting still completes with a clear degraded-mode notice or inlined result body, and the step summary records the failure.
- Existing fallback status update remains a last-resort safety net when generators fail.
- Error excerpts remain sanitized and bounded by the existing MAX_ERROR_LENGTH semantics.

- No failure path emits state markers in result comments.
- No-session failures do not attempt to render invalid result markers.

title: Thread-history result comments lifecycle
description:
## Goal
Implement the thread-history comment lifecycle described in docs/plans/agent-runner-thread-history-comments-plan.md as one coherent implementation PR. The action should always append a full per-run result comment to GitHub issue/PR threads when a Netlify session exists, while keeping the sticky status comment short, mutable, and authoritative for state recovery.

## Background
Today each @netlify trigger overwrites the sticky status comment, so prior run narratives disappear from the GitHub timeline. The existing PR-only history comment also grows without bound and can eventually hit GitHub's 65,536-character comment body limit. The new design splits comments into: one mutable status comment carrying durable state markers, immutable per-session result comments carrying full narratives, and a small PR-only history TOC linking to result comments.

## Non-negotiable constraints
- Preserve PR #17 state-recovery hardening: extract-agent-id and reconcileAgentState continue to read only the bot-authored status comment and same-repo PR body fallback.
- Result comments must never contain STATUS_COMMENT_MARKER, HISTORY_COMMENT_MARKER, RUNNER_ID_MARKER_PREFIX, or SESSION_DATA_MARKER_PREFIX anywhere in their body.
- No feature flag. Once shipped, the action always appends full result comments when comments are expected and a Netlify session exists.
- The implementation lands as one PR, though commits may be organized by area.

## Acceptance criteria
- A successful run posts a new immutable result comment, then updates the sticky status comment to link to it.
- A direct PR run updates/replaces one history TOC comment, newest-first, including a one-row TOC on the first result.
- Issue-created PR handoff leaves issue-local status/result comments and creates PR-local result/status/TOC comments.
- Preflight/setup failures with no session remain status-comment-only.
- Unit, scenario, docs, and release verification beads are complete.
notes:
Converted from docs/plans/agent-runner-thread-history-comments-plan.md on 2026-05-07.

Single-PR implementation graph:
- agent-runner-action-1zy: marker helpers and poisoning guards.
- agent-runner-action-3ha: truncation/status-body assembly primitives.
- agent-runner-action-9so: immutable result comment renderer.
- agent-runner-action-t3m: truncated sticky status renderer.
- agent-runner-action-tet: result comment posting helper and outputs.
- agent-runner-action-yag: newest-first PR history TOC.
- agent-runner-action-w5o: failure/fallback/no-session behavior.
- agent-runner-action-m03: direct issue/PR action.yml lifecycle wiring.
- agent-runner-action-o8t: issue-created PR cross-posting with PR-local result/status/TOC.
- agent-runner-action-xca: focused unit tests.
- agent-runner-action-t2e: scenario harness and simulator coverage.
- agent-runner-action-h3j: docs/security/step-summary lifecycle references.
- agent-runner-action-6io: final verification and release evidence.

The existing release gate agent-runner-action-o70 now depends on this feature bead so public refs remain blocked until this work and verification complete.

title: Replace growing history comment with newest-first result TOC
description:
## Goal
